newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rate cut just reward for govt-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy rate cut just reward for govt-Ciampi.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted as saying on Thursday that Italy's interest rate cut late Wednesday was a just reward for the government's policy of economic rigour.
"It is a victory, the concrete success of the coherent and rigorous policy that we have been following over several months," Ciampi said in an interview in Rome daily La Repubblica.
Ciampi also said it was important that commercial banks passed on the effect of the rate cut to corporate borrowers without delay.
The Bank of Italy cut Italy's discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 percent late Wednesday.
"The exposure of the entrepreneurial sector can be valued at 800 to 900 trillion lire," he said.

"To cut the discount rate by three quarters of a (percentage) point gives a good thrust towards recovery but it is important that market rates fall in line quickly with the Bank of Italy's decision," said Ciampi.
Ciampi reiterated the government's intention of taking the lira back into the European exchange rate mechanism by the end of the year as a precursor to joining a currency union.
"The objective of Ciampi is to reenter the ERM by the end of the year," he said.
Ciampi said Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio had taken action after he had seen inflation headed below three percent and a tough 1997 budget in the works.
"The lowering of the discount rate is the consequence," he said.
Ciampi warned against any attempts to water down the 1997 budget when it goes to parliament for a first reading at the end of this month.
"This budget must serve to enter Europe therefore I see the real risks in those who try to bend the budget towards different objectives," he added.

Preliminary consumer price inflation data from 10 Italian cities on Monday and Tuesday this week pointed towards an October inflation rate of three percent, but most analysts had believed Italy would hold back until November data showed inflation under three percent before cutting rates .
Ciampi said he had only learned of the cut 15 minutes before it was announced.
He said confidence was the key ingredient to sustained economic recovery.

"There is one thing that matters quite a lot more than any budget or any economic strategy. It is confidence. The country has to recover confidence in itself in order to recover the confidence of international markets," he said.
